findings.issue: The app ships with no test suite at all — no runner, no test script, no test files — despite the riskiest logic being pure functions that would be cheap to test.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest and cover app/lib/format.ts, the transform helpers and card builder in app/lib/api.server.ts, and the loaders' filter/sort logic with a stubbed fetch.

findings.issue: Search/type/generation filtering, 48-per-page slicing and page clamping are untested; a data-layer refactor (e.g. how typesById is built) would silently break filter results and pagination.
findings.suggestion: Extract the filtering/pagination into a pure function and test combined filters, empty results, page out of range, and boundary slices.

findings.issue: Sort comparator's missing-values-last-in-both-directions branch and name tie-break have no coverage; null ordering is the classic thing that inverts under refactor.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test sortRows against fixtures with null power/accuracy/category in ascending and descending directions, plus default level-up ordering.

findings.issue: Move grouping (method ordering, dedup key, default game = highest order, level column only for level-up, invalid ?game= fallback) is spec-critical and untested.
findings.suggestion: Test the loader against a small canned ApiPokemon/ApiMove fixture asserting table order, method ordering (Level Up, Machine, Egg, Tutor, then alphabetical) and game fallback.

findings.issue: cardsFromPokemon's alternate-form exclusion (id > 10000), dedup and dex-number sort — including the deoxys-normal → deoxys species mapping — have no failing signal.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with refs for species, forms above 10000, duplicates and a non-species id, including the ability-page hidden flag.

findings.issue: queryFor's URL-state serialization (omit empty/default, omit page<=1) is untested; a regression breaks deep links and the 'omit default parameters' requirement.
findings.suggestion: Table-driven tests over queryFor: empty filters, page 1, combined filters, all-defaults.

findings.issue: Localization helpers untested: latest-English flavor text takes the LAST en entry while short_effect takes the FIRST, plus the \n/\f whitespace collapse — flipping last/first would pass typecheck.
findings.suggestion: Test latestEnglishFlavorText and englishShortEffect with mixed-language entries and embedded newlines/form feeds.

findings.issue: Debounced-search/URL-sync logic (lastPushed ref, timer race, back/forward resync) is the most fragile client code and is only exercised by the acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: A Playwright component/E2E test typing in the search box asserting the URL updates after debounce and that back/forward restores the input.

findings.issue: 404 classification (NotFoundError → data(null, 404) → root ErrorBoundary 'Not found' heading) is unguarded; a refactor could render 'Something went wrong' for missing Pokémon or vice versa.
findings.suggestion: Test getRecord with a 404 response and the root errorHeading with a 404 vs 500 response.

findings.issue: The 60s in-memory cache (TTL, failure eviction) is untested; the acceptance harness's live-data overlay already runs close to staleness, and stale-data bugs would be intermittent and hard to reproduce.
findings.suggestion: Test that a rejected fetch evicts the entry and that expiry refetches, using an injectable clock.

summary: The app contains zero tests — no runner, no script, no test files — and its riskiest logic (filtering, pagination, sorting, URL state, data transforms) is entirely uncovered. The one mitigation is that the risky logic is cleanly factored into pure functions in app/lib and route loaders, so tests would be cheap to add. Until then, only the external acceptance suite stands between refactors and silent regressions.
